newsitem.title: DUBAI: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - premiums under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Mideast Gulf oil outlook - premiums under pressure.

text.p: A seasonal slowdown in demand continues to put pressure on the Gulf middle distillate market with premiums narrowing, Gulf traders said on Thursday.
Demand from India, which largely governs gas oil spot premiums in the Gulf, has eased in the past few weeks.
"India is not buying very much. Their 270,000-tonne June tender is the lowest for a very long time," said one trader.

Indian Oil Corp bought 270,000 tonnes of 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil in its last tender for June delivery. It also issued a tender to buy two 40,000- to 45,000-tonne cargoes of high speed diesel or 1.0 percent sulphur gas oil for July delivery.
"Gas oil premiums are very low in the Gulf. They are something like 25 cents for one percent sulphur and 35 cents for 0.5 percent sulphur," said a trader.
"Very little is being traded at the moment," he added.

Others said recent middle distillate tenders by the Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) were indicative of the fact that cargoes were struggling to find new homes. It also showed that some of ADNOC's term customers may have been lifting less than their contractual volumes.
"The result of ADNOC's tender for 75,000 tonnes of 0.5 percent gas oil will be known in the next three to four days. It is likely to be around 35 to 40 cents," one said.

Traders said premiums were likely to remain around 20-25 cents for one percent sulphur gas oil, down from 30-40 cents at the beginning of the month, and at between 35 and 40 cents on 0.5 percent gas oil from 60-65 cents previously.
The differential between Gulf and Mediterranean prices was also seen to be narrowing, to around $10 a tonne from about $35 previously, indicative of the soft Gulf market, traders said.
Gas oil was independently assessed at $23.25 a barrel fob Gulf from around $24.30 at the beginning of the month.
Traders said the Gulf spot market for kerosene was even weaker, mainly due to a summer slowdown in India.

But one trader said some customers had been taking advantage of soft prices to stock up in the Far East for winter demand. "People have been buying jet and taking it to Singapore, Subic Bay and even Guam. They are already stockpiling it for winter."
Premiums were seen at between 20 and 25 cents.
"It is very disappointing. India is not buying and Pakistan is only buying on a term basis, so there are not too many opportunities in kerosene," a trader said.
ADNOC has sold by tender 25,000 tonnes of jet fuel for June 4-6 lifting at 10 cents a barrel above spot Middle East quotes.

Previously ADNOC sold 25,000 tonnes of jet fuel to a U.S. trader at a premium of 25 cents for May 14-15 lifting, fob basis. Traders also said ADNOC had sold on a spot basis a similar sized jet fuel cargo for mid-June lifting at a premium of between 20 and 25 cents to a trader for export to India.
Kerosene was assessed at around $23 a barrel fob Gulf from $23.30 a fortnight earlier.
Meanwhile, Saudi Aramco expects to conclude term discussions with 13 oil firms by Friday, traders said.
